$description: Cosmos 2.3.0 base tokens, theme adapters and contrast pairs

void-edge.$description: Depth at the edge of the field

boundary.$description: Essential control outlines on dark surfaces

field.$description: Root depth behind every Deep Space screen. Opaque, so text is measured against void-edge and void.

nebula.$description: One atmospheric field per screen, behind the focal object or a section entry; never behind reading text.

corona.$description: The only glow: the halo of the single focal object, painted in a box four to six times its diameter.

accretion.$description: A 1–2 px ring around the focal object. Never progress, status or a control outline.

horizon.$description: Light lines of 1–2 px: the top light of a surface, the horizon ribbon, a section signature.

rim.$description: A 1 px border light for the focal or selected surface, beside its essential boundary rather than replacing it.

action.$description: Fill of the one primary action. The Void label passes on every stop.

spectrum.$description: The brand signature line. Category legends use solid labelled swatches instead.

float.$description: Floating surfaces: popovers, sheets, dialogs and device frames.

action.$description: Underglow of the one primary action at rest. Removed when disabled.

space.$description: Shared rhythm: 1 unit is 1 CSS px on web and 1 dp natively, so a client uses these numbers unchanged and never publishes its own table.

radius.$description: Web anchors. Android and Wear map the same roles to native geometry in platformAdapters (C09); the anchors are not copied into a native scale.

motion.$description: Durations are shared: 150 ms feedback, 300 ms local state, 500 ms context change. Each platform part adds its own easing set in platformAdapters (C30); easing here is the cross-platform standard.

layer.$description: Relative semantic stacking tier; use platform layer primitives for modal isolation.

starfield.$description: The deterministic edge star layer shared by every platform that draws one. Watch screens draw none.

band.$description: Outer band, as a fraction of each edge, where stars may sit. The central rectangle stays clear.

bucket.$description: Size quantum; a resize regenerates only when it crosses a bucket.

lowPowerFactor.$description: Share of stars drawn under low power, thermal pressure or a low-performance tier.

algorithm: Bucket: bw = ceil(width / bucket) * bucket and bh likewise, in CSS px or dp.
Seed: FNV-1a 32-bit over the UTF-8 bytes of "<surfaceId>@<bw>x<bh>"; random numbers come from mulberry32(seed) as uint32 / 2^32.
Count: round-half-up(bw * bh / areaPerStar) clamped to [min, max] for the surface kind.
Per star, in this order: one draw selects the magnitude, one the radius, one the alpha, one the color; then up to `attempts` (u, v) pairs.

Color: draw < inkShare is ink; otherwise accents[min(accents.length - 1, floor((draw - inkShare) / ((1 - inkShare) / accents.length)))], demoted to ink when that accent already holds floor(count * maxAccentShare) stars or all accents hold floor(count * (1 - inkShare)).

Position: reject (u, v) when both lie strictly inside (band, 1 - band), or when the squared bucket-pixel distance to an accepted star is below (2 * max(r, rOther))^2. A star with no accepted attempt is skipped.
Spikes: the first `maxSpikes` accepted bright stars carry a four-point diffraction cross 5 * r long.
Render at x = u * width, y = v * height. Exclusion zones filter accepted stars afterwards and never reseed.

watchAmbient.$description: watchAmbient semantic colors. A display profile publishes none of the interactive roles, so a control on this theme takes its colour from the profile it is not drawn in.

platformAdapters.$description: Radius, duration and easing per platform part, with the notation each part authors in and the geometry a native shape replaces. Spacing needs no mapping: 1 unit is 1 CSS px on web and 1 dp natively (C09).

webPage.$description: Long-form marketing and documentation pages. Shares the web radius anchors and the web easing set; a page needs a mapping of its own only if it introduces a role the anchors do not cover.

webApp.$description: Signed-in web application. Same web profile today; a divergence is recorded here rather than by editing the shared anchors.

android.$description: Compose applications. Radius is the part's own scale — control 8, secondary 10, emphasis 14, record 20, overlay 28 dp — because a handheld screen steps from a 48 dp target to a full-bleed overlay in five increments where a pointer surface needs three. Compose has no Oklab colour space, so this part reads the anchors and the profile roles in sRGB.

watch.$description: Wear OS round screens. There is no corner to measure on a round screen, so this part publishes shapes rather than a radius: control and record are round and an overlay is a capsule. The easing and duration sets are the Android ones by decision — the same scale at a much smaller physical size.

projection.$description: oklch projection of the anchors and of the semantic roles of the profiles this part runs, for authoring and theming. Derived from the sRGB value beside it, which stays the truth contrast is measured in (C29).

fetchWhen: pairing a translucent, blurred or layered surface
checking or changing a theme profile
contrastPairs.$description: Measured composited contrast per theme profile, with the guidance for each pair.

choosing between the tiers, or deciding whether a change animates at all
porting a transition to a native toolkit and proving curve parity
motionMotifs.$description: The named choreographies a state change animates with, per tier and per platform, with the curve parity fixture.

fetchWhen: building or changing any surface, before choosing a pattern
deciding which rules a component inherits and therefore which it must satisfy
porting a component to a native toolkit and finding the counterpart that exists
components.$description: The component index: which rules each component inherits, the theme roles and corner role it consumes, the states it can be in and the motif it moves with, sliced per platform part.
